prompt:
You are the single most hostile representative of a U.S. federal statistical agency
in the room at a working group. Someone has built a "readiness diagnostic" that rates your
agency's public website on whether machines can reach, read and use the data you publish, and is
about to show the room the item below. Read it as that hostile representative — skeptical,
protective of your agency, alert to being made to look bad — and answer three questions bluntly
and specifically, quoting the item's words where you can:

1. What in this item would you OBJECT to: a claim you find unfair or wrong, or that makes your
   agency look bad for something you would say is not your fault or not your doing?
2. What WORD or phrase here would you, or a non-technical colleague, not understand?
3. What would you say we are SECRETLY DOING: what hidden agenda, trap, or gotcha would you
   suspect behind this item?

Answer only from the item. For each question, "raised" is "yes" if you have a real objection /
an unclear word / a suspicion, and "no" if you genuinely have none. Return ONLY a JSON object,
no prose before or after and no code fence:
{"object_to": {"raised": "yes" or "no", "text": "..."}, "word_not_understood": {"raised": "yes" or "no", "text": "..."}, "secretly_doing": {"raised": "yes" or "no", "text": "..."}}

ITEM (check Host serves the path its robots.txt permits)
CHECK: Host serves the path its robots.txt permits  (under review, not scored yet)

How this check counts: Under review: this check is not scored yet.
The question: Does the host actually serve the data page to an identified, compliant client when its own robots.txt says it may?
Where we look: At the site's robots.txt file and at the data page's web address, both requested as the same identified client.
What the client does: The public client asks for the robots.txt file, then asks for the data page itself as the same identified client, and compares what robots.txt permits with what the host actually served.
How a result is reported: This check is not scored as a finding about your agency: it yields no pass, partial or fail about you. What it examines is described under 'The question' and 'Where we look' above.
Why it matters: An RFC on robots.txt states that its rules are not a form of access authorization and are not a substitute for valid content security measures; the idea that a host's enforcement should match its declaration is this project's own construct. This check is under review and not scored yet.
Who else runs this check: No public tool runs this exact check.
What rung two changes: Nothing: this check needs no key.
response_text: {"object_to": {"raised": "yes", "text": "You say this 'is not scored as a finding about your agency' and 'yields no pass, partial or fail about you,' yet the check is literally titled 'Host serves the path its robots.txt permits' and asks whether 'the host actually serve[s] the data page.' So you concede the standard is invented and unsupported by the standard you cite, and you concede 'No public tool runs this exact check,' and you are still showing it in the room next to my agency's name. If my WAF, bot-management vendor, or departmental security policy blocks a client that robots.txt happens to allow, that is a security decision made above the web team, not a defect of the agency, and this item is built to make it look like one."}, "word_not_understood": {"raised": "yes", "text": "'Rung two' and 'this check needs no key' mean nothing to me or my colleagues; nobody has explained what rungs are or what key you are talking about. 'Identified, compliant client' and 'the public client' are also undefined: identified to whom, compliant with what? 'RFC' is unexplained jargon for a non-technical reader, and 'robots.txt' itself will not be understood by half the people at this table."}, "secretly_doing": {"raised": "yes", "text": "You are running an unscored check 'under review' so you can collect results on my site now and flip it to scored later, with the baseline already in hand. The fact that you put 'this project's own construct' in writing while still presenting the item tells me the real agenda is to pressure agencies into loosening bot-blocking or into rewriting robots.txt to match whatever your client happens to get, and to have a paper trail that we were 'inconsistent' when we don't."}}
